<reason>CON (A) built the more coherent path: a single master-frame — the savings are counted on a metric (containment/cost-per-contact) that structurally cannot record the harms — advanced consistently across every speech. A killed B's best accountability point (generative outputs can't be grepped like a script, liability attaches per Air Canada, most wronged customers churn silently rather than sue), answered B's pipeline pressure question with a genuine mechanism B then dropped, and rebutted B's repeat-contact-metrics answer with the silent-churn invisibility point. Crucially, B's closing merely recapped "no comparative numbers" without engaging A's argument that B's own instruments cannot produce those numbers, leaving A's burden allocation (PRO must show costs fall MORE) live at the end. B's baseline-comparison frame ("compared to what?") and structural-savings case were genuinely strong and keep this competitive, but B lost the accountability exchange, dropped the pipeline, and failed to adapt late; the clipped opening was a minor execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A4.4 vs B4.1: B answered the containment critique by citing repeat-contact tracking as the "gave up" signal; A countered that the customer who simply never returns is invisible to those dashboards, so "we measure it" answers nothing — a rebuttal B's closing never addressed, neutralizing B's central no-numbers attack. Runner-up: A2.3's ungreppable-hallucination point dismantling B2.4's "fix one bad script" defense.</best_rebuttal>
